title: Taxim Gardens floor show: Harry Fleming and Belle Davis
summary: At Lehmann's Taxim Gardens, dancer Harry Fleming, formerly of Belle Davis's children's troupe in London, ran the floor show; Briggs explains Belle Davis and Scott & Whaley.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We doubled in -- he had a garden, another establishment, which he called the Taxim Gardens. He had the Petite Chaut. And the Taxim Gardens was further out, I'd say it's about two or three kilometers out from Constantinople.
And there he had a floor show, and this floor show, it was amazing. Harry Fleming who was a famous dancer, who I knew, he had come over with Belle Davis' Pickaninnys to
Briggs
England, way before the war. He had formed his own troupe and was traveling around, and --
What was that?
Belle Davis' Pickaninnys, I've never heard of that.
In London.
Was it a minstrel show, was it?

It was almost the same thing as the Jenkins Orphanage, you see. She had arranged with certain parents who had no means of having their children to learn how to dance, and different things. She, with the parents' authority, you see, she had taken them from America, to England. She had kind of a dance school.
I see. What was her name?
Belle Davis.
Adele?
Belle.
